haiku-low.q1: It returns 202 with the rejected list (position and reason), only after the log confirms the append. Malformed events are not stored; the rest of the batch is stored.
haiku-low.q2: It resends the same event_ids. Rejected events are never retried. Resends are safe because deduplication drops copies already known.
haiku-low.q3: The copy that is first in log order (log partition and offset) is kept in events_clean, in the partition for its received day. Later copies are dropped.
haiku-low.q4: Its day is the UTC date the collector received it, so Tuesday's partition, and Tuesday's replay covers it. The client timestamp is ignored for this.
haiku-low.q5: A key-value store holds dedup:{event_id}, written once after the first copy's output is durable. Old keys expire after an 8-day TTL. dedup_ledger records first log partition, offset, and received day, kept 90 days.
haiku-low.q7: Ledger inserts are insert-if-absent and events_clean writes are MERGEs on event_id, so repeats are absorbed. The dedup key is set only after both succeed, so a crashed batch is reprocessed.
haiku-low.q8: It reads archive records received on day D, joined to dedup_ledger first copies. Rebuilt rows are written to the shadow table events_clean_rebuild_D, then atomically swapped into events_clean.
haiku-low.q9: It keeps only archive records whose log partition and offset equal the ledger's first-copy entry. The ledger, kept 90 days, covers earlier-day first copies that the archive may have lost.
haiku-low.q10: Failed validation aborts and leaves events_clean untouched. The swap is atomic, so readers see old or new data. The shadow table is left behind. Operator recovery steps are NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: Closed UTC days, meaning at or after D+1 02:00 UTC, within 90 days of D, after live ingestion has passed D+1 02:00 on all partitions and the archive is sealed. Only one rebuild per day at a time.
haiku-low.q12: Undecided. Product must decide between dropping and keeping with a flag. The plan reserves an empty enrichment slot for it, and the archive keeps every copy.

sonnet.q1: It returns 202 only after the log confirms the append of the accepted events. The body includes the rejected list (malformed events with batch position and reason); malformed events are not stored, and the other events continue.
sonnet.q2: It resends the same event_ids (the whole batch). Resending is safe because deduplication drops known copies. Clients never retry rejected events.
sonnet.q3: The first copy by log order (offset) is written to events_clean, in the partition of that first copy's received day. Later copies are not written (kept only in the archive). Exception: a copy arriving after the 8-day TTL is treated live as a first copy and written to its own received day's partition, until a replay removes it.
sonnet.q4: Tuesday's partition (the UTC date of received_at, 00:10 Tuesday) and Tuesday's replay. The client timestamp is data only.
sonnet.q5: In the key-value store, as key dedup:{event_id}, written once when the first copy is processed (after the output is durable) and never refreshed. Entries are removed by the 8-day TTL. (The dedup_ledger warehouse table also records the first copy's log partition, offset, received day, for 90 days.)
sonnet.q7: The key-value key is set only after both warehouse writes (ledger insert-if-absent and MERGE on event_id) succeed. A crash before that leaves no key, so the batch is reprocessed; the insert-if-absent and MERGE absorb the repeats, so nothing is lost or duplicated.
sonnet.q8: A replay reads only the archive (records with received_at on D) and dedup_ledger. It writes rebuilt rows to the shadow table events_clean_rebuild_D, which dashboards never read.
sonnet.q9: It joins archive records for D to dedup_ledger on event_id and keeps a record only if its (log partition, log offset) equals the ledger's first-copy partition and offset. This drops later copies on D and copies whose first copy arrived on an earlier day.
sonnet.q10: events_clean is left untouched: validation failures abort before the swap, and the swap is a single atomic partition replace, so dashboards see only the old data; only the shadow table may remain. The operator's recovery steps are NOT STATED.
sonnet.q11: Closed days (at or after D+1 02:00 UTC) that are within 90 days, whose live ingestion has passed D+1 02:00 on every partition, whose archive is sealed (manifests exist, archiver past live watermark), and with no other rebuild of D running. The current open day cannot be replayed.
sonnet.q12: Not decided (open item 1): drop or keep with a flag is undecided. The plan only reserves an empty slot in the enrich step; the archive keeps every copy either way, and a deterministic rule could be applied by replay within 90 days.
